characters.name: Jonathan Harker
characters.notes: Young solicitor sent to Transylvania to close a property sale. Imprisoned by the Count; later marries Mina.

characters.name: Mina Murray
characters.notes: Jonathan's fiancée, then wife. Schoolteacher with a sharp mind — compiles the group's journals into one narrative.

characters.name: Lucy Westenra
characters.notes: Mina's dearest friend. Courted by three men at once. The Count's first English victim.

characters.name: Dr. John Seward
characters.notes: Young asylum director. One of Lucy's rejected suitors. Keeps a phonograph diary.

characters.name: Arthur Holmwood
characters.notes: Lucy's fiancé, later Lord Godalming. Devoted, and devastated by what he must do to save her soul.

characters.name: Quincey Morris
characters.notes: American adventurer, another of Lucy's suitors. Blunt, brave, ultimately self-sacrificing.

characters.name: Abraham Van Helsing
characters.notes: Dutch physician and scholar. Recognizes the vampire for what it is when no one else will.

characters.name: Count Dracula
characters.notes: Centuries-old nobleman of Transylvania. Charming host, ancient predator.

characters.name: Renfield
characters.notes: Patient at Seward's asylum. Eats insects to absorb their 'life.' Unknowingly in the Count's thrall.

locations.name: Bistritz
locations.notes: Transylvanian town where Jonathan's coach journey begins.

locations.name: Borgo Pass
locations.notes: Mountain pass where the Count's own carriage meets Jonathan at midnight.

locations.name: Castle Dracula
locations.notes: The Count's crumbling ancestral seat. No mirrors, no servants, no way out.

locations.name: Whitby
locations.notes: Yorkshire seaside town. Where the Demeter runs aground and Lucy first falls under the Count's shadow.

locations.name: Hillingham
locations.notes: Lucy and her mother's home outside London.

locations.name: Purfleet Asylum
locations.notes: Dr. Seward's asylum, adjoining the Count's newly-purchased Carfax estate.

locations.name: Carfax Estate
locations.notes: The derelict property the Count has bought — and filled with boxes of his native earth.

locations.name: Budapest
locations.notes: Where Jonathan is found, feverish and raving, after his escape.

locations.name: Transylvania (Return)
locations.notes: The Count's homeland, reached again in the final pursuit.

themes.name: Ancient Evil vs. Modern Science
themes.notes: Diaries, typewriters, blood transfusions, telegrams — and none of it enough without old-world faith.

themes.name: Blood and Contagion
themes.notes: Blood as life, as corruption, as the thing passed from victim to victim.

themes.name: Faith and the Sacred
themes.notes: Crucifixes, communion wafers, holy water — belief as a weapon when science fails.

themes.name: The New Woman
themes.notes: Mina's competence and Lucy's desire read as dangerous, then as the thing that saves everyone.

themes.name: Found Family and Fellowship
themes.notes: Strangers and rivals for Lucy's hand become a single, unbreakable circle.

themes.name: Purity and Corruption
themes.notes: What the Count takes from Lucy and Mina isn't only blood.

misc.name: The Demeter's Log
misc.notes: The wrecked ship's captain lashed himself to the wheel rather than abandon his post.

misc.name: Boxes of Consecrated Earth
misc.notes: Fifty boxes of Transylvanian soil, shipped to Carfax — the Count's only safe resting places in England.

misc.name: Van Helsing's Bag
misc.notes: Garlic, crucifixes, a stake and hammer, communion wafers — old-world tools for a very old evil.

misc.name: Jonathan's Shorthand Journal
misc.notes: Written in shorthand so the Count couldn't read it. The first hard evidence of what he is.

misc.name: Mina's Typewritten Compilation
misc.notes: Every diary, letter, and phonograph cylinder, cross-referenced and dated into one document.

misc.name: The Communion Wafer
misc.notes: Used to seal the boxes of earth — and, devastatingly, to mark Mina's own forehead.

scenes.title: Jonathan Departs for Transylvania
scenes.summary: Jonathan sets out to finalize the Count's London property purchase, noting the local dread the trip provokes.

scenes.title: Warnings at the Borgo Pass
scenes.summary: Villagers press a crucifix on Jonathan and cross themselves at the mention of the Count. His carriage meets him at midnight, driven by an unseen hand.

scenes.title: Arrival at Castle Dracula
scenes.summary: The Count receives Jonathan with unsettling grace — cold hands, no servants in sight, and food only for his guest.

scenes.title: No Mirrors, No Reflection
scenes.summary: Jonathan realizes the castle has not one mirror, and that his host casts no reflection at all.

scenes.title: Jonathan Realizes He's a Prisoner
scenes.summary: Every door is locked from outside. Jonathan begins keeping his journal in shorthand, the only lock the Count can't pick.

scenes.title: The Three Weird Women
scenes.summary: Three pale women corner Jonathan in the moonlight. The Count intervenes at the last second: "This man belongs to me."

scenes.title: Dracula Departs Wearing Jonathan's Clothes
scenes.summary: Fifty boxes of earth are loaded for shipment. Jonathan watches the Count descend the castle wall like a lizard — dressed, unmistakably, in Jonathan's own suit.

scenes.title: Jonathan's Desperate Escape
scenes.summary: Jonathan climbs the same wall to escape the castle he cannot otherwise leave, and is later found raving in a Budapest hospital, his journal clutched shut.

scenes.title: Lucy and Mina's Correspondence
scenes.summary: Letters between the two friends: Mina's shorthand practice for Jonathan's sake, and Lucy's news of not one but three proposals in a single day.

scenes.title: Lucy Accepts Arthur's Proposal
scenes.summary: Lucy chooses Arthur, gently turning down Dr. Seward and Quincey Morris, who both take it with more grace than she expected.

scenes.title: Mina Joins Lucy in Whitby
scenes.summary: Mina arrives at the seaside for a long visit, worried about Lucy's recent sleepwalking and about Jonathan's silence.

scenes.title: The Demeter Wrecks at Whitby
scenes.summary: A Russian schooner runs aground in a sudden storm, her captain lashed dead to the wheel and every hand lost. A great dark shape bounds ashore. Reported secondhand -- no one in the group witnesses it directly.

scenes.title: Lucy Begins Sleepwalking
scenes.summary: Mina finds Lucy's bed empty at midnight and follows her to the churchyard, where a dark figure bends over her before slipping away.

scenes.title: Lucy's Health Declines
scenes.summary: Back at Hillingham, Lucy grows pale and listless. Arthur, alarmed, asks Dr. Seward to examine her.

scenes.title: Dr. Seward Summons Van Helsing
scenes.summary: Baffled by two small puncture wounds that won't heal, Seward wires his old teacher — a man who believes in things Seward doesn't.

scenes.title: Renfield's Strange Fixation
scenes.summary: Seward's patient Renfield catalogs flies, then spiders, then birds — each fed to the next, climbing toward something he calls 'the Master.'

scenes.title: The First Blood Transfusion
scenes.summary: Van Helsing arrives, examines Lucy's wounds in silence, and gives Arthur his own blood to save her — telling him almost nothing of why.

scenes.title: Van Helsing's Garlic and Warnings
scenes.summary: Van Helsing wreathes Lucy's room in garlic flowers and begs her mother never to remove them, without explaining why.

scenes.title: Lucy's Mother Removes the Garlic
scenes.summary: Not knowing what it protects against, Lucy's mother clears the flowers away for the night air — the one night Van Helsing isn't there to stop her.

scenes.title: Lucy Dies
scenes.summary: Despite three transfusions and every precaution, Lucy slips away in the night — and, for one unsettling moment before the end, seems almost to smile with teeth too sharp.

scenes.title: The Bloofer Lady Preys on Children
scenes.summary: Newspapers report a beautiful woman luring small children from Hampstead Heath at night. Van Helsing tells Seward, plainly, who it is.

scenes.title: Jonathan and Mina Return, Married
scenes.summary: Recovered at last, Jonathan marries Mina in Budapest, and the two return to England together — his journal still unread by anyone but him.

scenes.title: Staking Lucy in Her Tomb
scenes.summary: Arthur drives the stake through the thing wearing Lucy's face, at Van Helsing's insistence, so her soul can finally rest.

scenes.title: Mina Compiles the Documents
scenes.summary: Mina types every diary and letter into one continuous, dated account — and is the first to notice how the pieces actually fit together.

scenes.title: Renfield Attacked, Warns the Group
scenes.summary: Battered and dying alone in his cell, Renfield finally understands what the Master next door has been using him for -- moments too late for anyone to hear his warning.

scenes.title: Dracula Attacks Mina
scenes.summary: The men break into the Harkers' room to find the Count forcing Mina to drink his own blood — and know, watching, exactly what it means.

scenes.title: Destroying the Boxes of Earth
scenes.summary: The group hunts down and sterilizes every box of Transylvanian soil the Count shipped to England, cutting off his safe harbors one by one.

scenes.title: The Pursuit to Transylvania
scenes.summary: With Mina marked and weakening by the day, the group races the Count back toward his own castle before winter closes the passes.

scenes.title: Race Against the Setting Sun
scenes.summary: Local guards escort the Count's coffin on its final leg home. The group intercepts it with minutes of daylight left.

scenes.title: Dracula's Destruction
scenes.summary: A knife through the heart and a throat cut in the same instant turn the Count to dust — but not before Quincey Morris falls defending them.

revealsLib.label: Renfield's fits are the Count announcing his arrival
